title: Every part
has a place.
hero.summary: Inventatory is a free, open-source inventory for electronics. Scan a vendor bag and it fills in the part and gives it a slot. Build a board and it walks you to every part.

film.title: Here's how it works
film.summary: A part comes in, the scanner reads its bag, and Inventatory fills it in from the vendor and gives it a slot. When a board needs it, you go straight there. The whole loop, in under two minutes.

title: It lives in
your terminal.
app.summary: One keyboard-driven window for stock, racks, orders, boards and history. Your inventory stays on your own computer. Pick a feature to see it at work on a real bench.

items.title: Search and count stock
items.text: Filter by part, category, parameter, location or SKU. Set a reorder threshold for each part and run a guided stocktake.
items.shot: Search “10k” at the keyboard; cut to the bag in its slot.

items.title: Give every part a slot
items.text: Assign parts to a 5 × 5 rack grid, so a location reads R1-B3 instead of Drawer 12. Print labels for slots and parts.
items.shot: The rack on screen, then the real rack: the slot found, the drawer pulled.

items.title: Import an order
items.text: Load a DigiKey order CSV and review each line. Accept or skip it, and accepted parts are created and filled in from DigiKey.
items.shot: Vendor bags scanned with the Scanner R1, one after another; each lands in the app.

items.title: Build a board from its BOM
items.text: Import a KiCad BOM to see what is in stock and what needs ordering. Pick the parts rack by rack, then deduct them from stock.
items.shot: A board’s parts list; hands walk from slot to slot picking each part.

items.title: Restore and undo
items.text: Every change is recorded with its before and after values. Set checkpoints, and restore or reverse a change, even after a restart.
items.shot: A wrong pick, one key, undone; the count comes back.
